narrative: The model estimated a 29% probability that you would be a bad credit risk. Although that is below a coin-flip, it is above the risk limit applied to this decision, so your loan application was denied. The most influential factor was the stated purpose of the loan: a business use, which is relatively uncommon among approved applicants (about 9% versus 35% for radio/TV), and this factor actually pushed the estimate toward good credit. The second most important factor was your checking account status. A balance in the 0-200 DM range is less common among approved applicants than having no checking account (about 18% versus 59%), and this pushed the estimate toward bad credit. The third factor was your time at your present residence: four years, compared with an approved-applicant average of about three years, and this also pushed toward good credit. So the denial was not driven by one overwhelming negative signal; rather, the checking-account signal was the main factor moving you toward bad credit, while the business purpose and residential stability moved you in the safer direction, but not enough to meet the lending rule. To improve your chances, consider applying with a stronger checking-account position, reducing the requested amount or term, and asking the lender what specific threshold you need to meet before reapplying.
